boards.title: Your First Weekend at Trinity University, Shared as Cards
boards.description: A low-key first-weekend sequence that begins on campus and makes room for a nearby public park.

cards.title: Start at Coates Student Center
cards.subtitle: First stop · Trinity campus
cards.notes: Use the student-center hub as a meeting point, then check its posted information and orient yourself before choosing the next stop.
cards.short_summary: Begin with a central campus rendezvous.
cards.evidence_claim: Trinity describes the Coates Student Center as a hub of campus life and identifies student-life services and multipurpose spaces there.
cards.access_notes: Building hours and room access are subject to change; check posted information on arrival.

cards.title: Get your bearings at Coates Library
cards.subtitle: Early weekend · Trinity campus
cards.notes: Take a quiet lap through the library, locate research help, and save the study-room reservation page for a later academic need.
cards.short_summary: A calm campus stop with research and study services.
cards.evidence_claim: Coates Library lists research services, study-room reservations, and opportunities to meet with a librarian.
cards.access_notes: Use library policies and posted access information when you visit.

cards.title: Walk through Chapman Center
cards.subtitle: Campus architecture stop · Trinity campus
cards.notes: Pass through this renovated academic building and notice how its shared spaces connect social sciences, business, and applied technology.
cards.short_summary: See a renewed O’Neil Ford-designed academic center.
cards.evidence_claim: Trinity says the O’Neil Ford-designed Chapman Center provides cross-disciplinary collaboration for social sciences, business, and applied technology.
cards.access_notes: Use public circulation areas only and follow any building-access signage.

cards.entity_name: Center for the Sciences and Innovation
cards.title: Find the Center for the Sciences and Innovation
cards.subtitle: Midday campus walk · Trinity campus
cards.notes: Add CSI to your campus loop so you can recognize the science complex and its Marrs McLean Hall connection on the directory.
cards.short_summary: Put Trinity’s science complex on your mental map.
cards.evidence_claim: Trinity’s campus directory lists the Center for the Sciences and Innovation and Marrs McLean Hall among its study and exploration spaces.
cards.source_title: Campus Buildings | Campus Directory | Trinity University
cards.access_notes: Follow campus wayfinding and respect restricted instructional or laboratory areas.

cards.title: Plan a meal at Mabee Dining Hall
cards.subtitle: Meal break · Trinity campus
cards.notes: Check the dining site for the current menu and service details, then choose a meal window that fits your orientation and campus plans.
cards.short_summary: Use the named dining hall to plan a practical meal break.
cards.evidence_claim: Trinity lists Mabee Dining Hall among its on-campus dining options and directs visitors to its dining website for locations, hours, menus, and services.
cards.source_title: Campus Buildings | Campus Directory | Trinity University
cards.access_notes: Consult Trinity Dining for current service details; payment or meal-plan requirements may apply.

cards.title: Pause at Parker Chapel
cards.subtitle: Reflective stop · Trinity campus
cards.notes: Visit the chapel exterior or attend an appropriate open program, keeping the space’s worship and reflection purpose in mind.
cards.short_summary: A nondenominational spiritual and cultural campus landmark.
cards.evidence_claim: Trinity identifies Margarite B. Parker Chapel as a nondenominational spiritual and cultural hub at the center of campus.
cards.source_title: Weddings at Parker Chapel | Chapel and Spiritual Life | Trinity University
cards.access_notes: Interior availability may depend on services or events; keep noise low and follow chapel guidance.

cards.title: Locate Laurie Auditorium
cards.subtitle: Plan ahead · Trinity campus
cards.notes: Find this performance venue during daylight so you know where to return if a university lecture, concert, or program interests you.
cards.short_summary: Get oriented to a named campus auditorium.
cards.evidence_claim: Trinity’s campus directory lists Laurie Auditorium among its performance venues, theaters, galleries, and studios.
cards.source_title: Campus Buildings | Campus Directory | Trinity University
cards.access_notes: Entry depends on the event and venue operations; consult the relevant event listing before attending.

cards.title: Mark the Ruth Taylor Fine Arts Center
cards.subtitle: Arts stop · Trinity campus
cards.notes: Walk by the fine-arts center and note Stieren Theater for a future ticketed or university-hosted performance, recital, or presentation.
cards.short_summary: Identify Trinity’s fine-arts and theater destination.
cards.evidence_claim: Trinity identifies the Ruth Taylor Fine Arts Center as the site of music recitals and concerts and identifies Stieren Theater as a venue for productions and events.
cards.source_title: Host an Event | Conferences and Special Programs | Trinity University
cards.access_notes: Event admission and venue access vary; verify an event’s details before going inside.

cards.title: Find Bell Athletic Center
cards.subtitle: Active-campus stop · Trinity campus
cards.notes: Add the athletic center to your walking route and check university recreation or athletics information before using any facility or attending an event.
cards.short_summary: Orient yourself to a named campus fitness and athletics space.
cards.evidence_claim: Trinity’s campus directory lists Bell Athletic Center among campus fitness facilities and places to relax or play.
cards.source_title: Campus Buildings | Campus Directory | Trinity University
cards.access_notes: Facility use and event entry can have eligibility or ticket requirements; check current university guidance.

cards.title: Close with a Brackenridge Park walk
cards.subtitle: Off-campus daylight stop · San Antonio
cards.notes: Take a daylight walk on the park paths, pause by the river, and use the official map to choose a comfortable return route.
cards.short_summary: Finish the weekend sequence in a large nearby public park.
cards.evidence_claim: The Brackenridge Park Conservancy states that the 343-acre park has tree-lined paths, picnic areas, and 2.2 miles along the San Antonio River, and is free and open daily from 5 a.m. to 11 p.m.
cards.source_title: Brackenridge Park Conservancy | Visit the Park
cards.access_notes: The Conservancy lists the park as free and open 5 a.m.–11 p.m. daily; use daylight awareness and follow park rules.
